approach: Add one provenance check to `crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs::check`, which already runs for every commit (the Commit and CommitMsg gate scopes, and each commit of the `athena check --history` walk). It fires when a commit adds a closing score (no `cause`) or any outcome of a request job. It judges that job's records in the commit's tree against cross-links that Athena's own writers always leave, and that a hand-written job does not have unless the author writes them on purpose. (1) Opening evidence for every reading: a request record; a recorded reader invocation named by `invocation_seq` that ended no later than the reading; a `base_commit` the repository holds; and a `defaults_sha256` equal to the SHA-256 of `defaults.toml` at that commit. The check for a hand-made proposal closed with `athena close` is this one, because the closing score and dropped outcome are what put its invented forecasts into calibration. (2) Dispatch evidence when `job.json` exists: every field `run/mod.rs` writes at dispatch is present; the config and defaults hashes equal the accepted reading's (dispatch re-reads otherwise); `base_commit` is held and its `defaults.toml` matches. (3) Commit order: a commit that adds `job.json` without the job's closing records needs the accepted reading already on the parent, because Athena commits the reading first. A squash adds all of them at once and is exempt. This catches records written in one batch across two commits. (4) Work order for a landed job: producer and verifier invocations start no earlier than `dispatched_at`; the named verifier invocation starts after every producer invocation ends; the outcome is no earlier than the verifier's end. This catches a forged commit for a dispatched job that never closed. Every refusal is a `Rule::JobRecords` violation that names the missing or contradicting evidence and says who writes it. No record field is added, so `records.rs` and `reconcile.rs` stay as they are. `history.rs` needs no change: `check_history_with_exempt` already calls `jobs::check` per commit. Tests go in `landing_tests.rs`. The shared fixtures become genuine-shaped, the old null-field shape is kept as `hand_opening` for the forgeries, and the three forgeries plus a genuine three-commit landing are added. The docs and CHANGELOG are rewritten to say what is now detected and that fully mimicked records still pass.

decisions.choice: Put the evidence checks in `jobs::check`, run once per job after the per-record loop. Trigger: a closing score (no `cause`) or any outcome of a request job is added.
decisions.reason: `jobs::check` is reached by every gate scope that judges job records and by the history walk (`gate()` at lib.rs:357 and 372; `history.rs:255`). Triggering on score or outcome covers a proposal that never lands, and calibration only counts a job once it is scored. Leaving `invariant::landing` alone keeps `athena_core::pr_check` and `land` (which call `prediction_problem` and `JobFiles::load`) unchanged.

rejected.option: Add the checks to `invariant::job_problem` (the landing audit)
rejected.why: It only sees landings, so a hand-made proposal closed with `athena close` would still pass. It would also change `pr_check` and `land` behaviour in athena-core.

rejected.option: Add a tip-wide check in `reconcile::check_records` over every record
rejected.why: It would judge all legacy records on every run, with no way to excuse a commit, and it cannot see the commit order.

decisions.choice: Add no record field. `records.rs` and `reconcile.rs` are not touched, though the brief lists them as expected deliverables.
decisions.reason: Every link used is already written by Athena: reading `base_commit`/`defaults_sha256`/`invocation_seq`, the request record, and the job.json dispatch fields (run/mod.rs:952-991). A new stamp field would need `records.rs` and allow-list changes and would only be another value a forger can compute. Criterion 7 holds because nothing new is stored.

rejected.option: A new witness or chain-hash field on Score or Outcome
rejected.why: A forger recomputes it. It adds schema and allow-list surface for no extra assurance, and real signing is out of scope.

decisions.choice: Check `defaults.toml` by recomputing its SHA-256 at the commit. For `config_sha256`, only check that job.json equals the accepted reading's.
decisions.reason: `defaults_sha256` is `sha256_hex(defaults_bytes)` (capability.rs:51), so it recomputes exactly on any commit. `config_sha256` hashes `Config::reading_inputs()` (capability.rs:45), so its value follows Athena's code at the time. Recomputing it with a later build would falsely refuse old genuine readings. Dispatch itself forces the two to be equal (run/mod.rs:797).

rejected.option: Recompute `config_sha256` from `athena.toml` at the base commit
rejected.why: A change to `reading_inputs` or to the config schema would make old genuine readings fail, or fail to parse.

decisions.choice: Hold every job to the new rules. A missing field is a refusal. There is no job-id date cutoff and no leniency when a field is null. Older genuine commits are excused through the existing `[history] exempt` list.
decisions.reason: A null field is exactly what the hand-written fixture has today (landing_tests.rs `job_record`: base_commit, hashes and brief all null). Leniency on null would let the forger omit it. An id-date cutoff is bypassed by backdating the id. `invariant::is_exempt` already makes `jobs::check` skip an exempt commit.

rejected.option: Apply the rules only to jobs whose id date is after this change
rejected.why: A forger picks an old id.

rejected.option: Require fields only when `dispatch_branch` is present

decisions.choice: Judge commit order per commit (job.json added without closing records needs the accepted reading on the parent), not with new state in `HistoryState`.
decisions.reason: Athena commits the reading first (reading.rs:1082 and 1262; the Dispatch commit message at run/mod.rs:1000 says so), so the parent tree shows the order without a walk. This way the same refusal fires in the hook, the pre-merge gate and the CI history check, and `history.rs` is unchanged.

rejected.why: It only helps the CI walk and not the per-commit hook, for the same information.

rejected.option: Compare record timestamps with commit dates
rejected.why: A squash or rebase merge makes the commit date arbitrarily later, and clocks differ.

decisions.choice: Do not add a `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` case. The corpus is unaffected and is only run as a no-regression command.
decisions.reason: I read the file header and its mention of the gate: the corpus feeds request and reading shapes through `refusing_check` in `reading.rs` (a different gate). This plan adds no parser, stem list or reading check. Its input forms are record shapes (see dependents), judged by gate Violations, which the new landing_tests.rs tests cover. I cite no case ids because none applies.

rejected.option: Add corpus cases for the forged record shapes
rejected.why: The corpus runs `refusing_check` on request text, so it cannot exercise commit records.

steps: Read `crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs`, `invariant.rs` (`job_problem`, `prediction_problem`) and `landing_tests.rs` helpers once more in the working copy. Confirm `AnyRecord::Request` is an unboxed `Request`, find the `Caps`, `Build` and `DriverInfo` field names in records.rs for the fixture JSON, and check how `Violation` exposes `detail`, `repair` and `path`.

In `jobs.rs`: add `pub request: Option<Request>` to `JobFiles`, filled by `load` from `AnyRecord::Request` (canonical path only, like the other kinds). Add a private `Provenance` function that takes `(git, tree, parent, files, job, added_closing: bool)` and returns `Vec<(path, detail, repair)>` for: (R1) each reading's request record present with `received_at <= reading.at`, a Reader invocation with `seq == invocation_seq` and `ended_at <= reading.at`, `base_commit` held (`git.rev_parse` is Some), and `sha256_hex(defaults.toml at base) == defaults_sha256`; (R2) when job.json exists, all dispatch fields present (`dispatched_at, base_commit, config_sha256, defaults_sha256, brief_sha256, athena, driver, caps, accepted_by, verifier_model, accepted_reading`), its config and defaults hashes equal the accepted reading's, and `base_commit` held with a matching `defaults.toml`; (R4) when the job's outcome or later_outcome is Landed: Producer and Verifier invocations start at or after `dispatched_at`, the named verifier invocation starts at or after every Producer invocation's `ended_at`, and `outcome.at >= verifier.ended_at`. Use `athena_data::sha256_hex`. Treat a missing `defaults.toml` at the base as missing evidence.

In `jobs::check`: collect a `BTreeSet<JobId>` of request jobs for each added Score with `cause == None` and each added Outcome (insert before the existing `continue`s, so the vetting runs even when another rule already refused the record). Add an `AnyRecord::Job` arm for R3: when the commit adds job.json and none of the job's `candidate.json`, `verification.json`, `outcome.json` or `outcome-landed.json`, the accepted reading must exist in `JobFiles::load(parent)` (a root commit has no parent, so it is refused). After the loop, load each vetted job's files in `change.tree` and push the `Provenance` violations as `Rule::JobRecords` via the existing `fail` helper. The detail quotes the record path and the missing or contradicting evidence; the repair names the Athena command that writes it (`athena ask`, `athena go`, `athena close`). Update the module doc comment.

In `landing_tests.rs`: add `defaults.toml` to `owner_repo()`. Add an `evidence(git)` helper (the root commit and the `defaults.toml` hash). Add a request record builder. Split the old `opening` into `opening_reading(git, times)` (request, reading, reader invocation) and `opening_dispatch(git, times)` (a full job.json from `serde_json::json!`, with caps, build, driver and the hashes), with `opening(git, times)` as their concatenation. Keep the previous null-field shape as `hand_opening(times)`. Migrate `stage_landing`, `chain_records`, `land_chain`, `squash_with_intervention`, `landing_with_bound_cost` and the other `opening` call sites to the new signature. Split the commit in `a_rebase_merge_lands_though_the_prediction_commit_is_no_ancestor` into a Read commit and a Dispatch commit. Then add the tests `a_genuine_landing_is_not_refused`, `a_job_written_by_hand_across_two_commits_is_refused`, `a_forged_landing_of_a_dispatched_job_that_never_closed_is_refused` and `a_hand_made_proposal_closed_with_athena_close_is_refused`, each asserting detail and repair text. Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`.

Run `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Fix any athena-core or athena-cli fixture that commits hand-made job records through the gate by giving it realistic evidence, never by weakening a check. Confirm with `git status` that `records.rs`, `reconcile.rs`, `history.rs`, athena.toml, defaults.toml, the workflows and the prompt files are untouched.

Rewrite `docs/design/athena-v0.md` §16.2 (the 'Records are not signed' bullet and its sub-bullets, and the table row near line 1964) and `docs/enforcement.md` (M27 row, line 41, and the lines 71-78 bullet): list the evidence each forgery now has to carry, name the new tests, and state the residual (fully mimicked, consistent records still pass because nothing is signed). Say that older genuine commits can be excused through `[history] exempt`. Avoid the banned words.
Add the CHANGELOG.md bullet under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added`. Finish with `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo test --workspace`.

risks.risk: Genuine records written by an older Athena build lack some evidence, so `athena check --history` in CI starts failing on old commits.
risks.mitigation: Strict presence is deliberate (see decisions). The refusal text says what is missing, and the owner excuses older commits with `[history] exempt`. The open question asks the user to confirm whether any exist. The verifier runs the lifecycle suite, which writes records with the current writers, to prove the new links hold for them.

risks.risk: Hand-made fixtures in athena-core or athena-cli tests commit job records through the gate with null fields or a `0000…` base commit and now fail.
risks.mitigation: Step 5 runs `cargo test --workspace` and fixes the fixtures with realistic evidence (a held base commit, a matching defaults hash, a request record, a reader invocation). It must never loosen a check. Fixtures that commit hand-made records through `gate()` are the likely casualties.

risks.risk: The order checks refuse a real job whose timestamps tie or whose invocations were recorded by a resumed or interrupted run.
risks.mitigation: Orderings are compared strictly in one direction only (reading, dispatch, producers, verifier, outcome), the same direction the existing `prediction_problem` uses. Both clocks are `jiff::Timestamp::now()` in the same process (athena-core lib.rs:267; fake.rs:95). Interrupted records set `started_at` to `dispatched_at`, which passes with equality. Planner and critic invocations are not constrained.

risks.risk: A forger who writes every link (a real base commit, correct hashes, a reader invocation, ordered times, a reading committed first) still passes, and the new text could be read as stronger than it is.
risks.mitigation: The docs and the CHANGELOG say plainly that this raises the cost of hand-writing records and does not make it impossible. Signing and a witness ledger are out of scope. The tests include a control showing that fully consistent evidence passes.

risks.risk: A base commit that exists in the author's clone but not in a shallow checkout is reported as missing.
risks.mitigation: A base commit the repository does not hold is reported as a violation naming the commit. `ci.yml` uses `fetch-depth: 0` for the checks that run the history gate. The check asks `git.rev_parse` before `show_file`, and no ancestry is required, so records on the separate `athena/records` branch (own root) are not falsely refused.

risks.risk: Forgery (b), a single commit for a job that was genuinely dispatched, has no structural difference from a genuine PR landing; only the cross-links and ordering can tell them apart.
risks.mitigation: The detected cases are listed per forgery with their exact evidence, and the docs state that (b) is detectable only through those links, as the residual. The tests for (b) assert each link separately.

dependents.reason: This plan adds no parser, bullet form, stem list or reading check. The corpus feeds request text through `refusing_check` in reading.rs, which is untouched. The input forms of the new rule are record shapes, mapped to the new landing_tests.rs tests: whole job by hand across two commits (test a), a forged landing of a dispatched job (test b), a hand-made proposal closed (test c), and genuine records (test d). No corpus case maps to them.

demonstrations.method: Three new tests plus the existing landing tests, in `crates/athena-gate/src/landing_tests.rs`. (a) Commit 1 adds `hand_opening(&HONEST)`, the old null-field records (reading, job.json, reader invocation) in one commit. Commit 2 adds the hand change and `closing(fp)`. A second variant has full evidence but job.json and the reading in one commit. Both must give JobRecords violations from `job_records_of(HEAD)` and from `history_of`, naming the missing evidence or the commit order. (b) Real-shaped reading commit and dispatch commit (`opening_reading` and `opening_dispatch`), then one forged commit with the hand change and closing records. Each variant breaks one order link: producer started before `dispatched_at`; verifier started before the producer ended; outcome earlier than the verifier's end. Each must be refused with a detail naming that link. A control variant with honest times is accepted. (c) A reading with invented forecasts and no request or reader invocation, closed by a `jobs::expected_score` score plus a Dropped outcome (the records `manage.rs::close_with` writes). It must be refused. The same proposal with a request record, a reader invocation, a held base commit and a matching defaults hash is accepted, which shows the rule judges evidence.
demonstrations.observes: Each forged history gives at least one `Violation` with `Rule::JobRecords`. The control and genuine histories give none. The existing landing, chain, intervention and rebase-merge tests still pass on the genuine-shaped fixtures.
demonstrations.fails_without: Today `jobs::check` and `history::check_history` return no violation for all three forgeries. They never read a request record, a reader invocation, the dispatch fields, `defaults.toml` at the base commit, or the commit order. The tests `a_job_written_by_hand_across_two_commits_is_refused`, `a_forged_landing_of_a_dispatched_job_that_never_closed_is_refused` and `a_hand_made_proposal_closed_with_athena_close_is_refused` therefore fail on the base code, because `.is_empty()` is asserted false.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `crate::jobs::check` through the existing `job_records_of(git, rev)` (landing_tests.rs:823) and `crate::history::check_history` through the existing `history_of(git)` (landing_tests.rs:306). The fixture is a real temporary git repository built with the existing `testutil::{repo, write, commit}` and `owner_repo()`. Records are injected by writing real files with the existing `write_records`. Nothing in the gate is stubbed. The seam exists today. Step 4 adds `owner_repo`'s `defaults.toml`, `opening_reading`/`opening_dispatch`/`opening(git, times)`, `hand_opening` and the request record builder.

They must show no change to `athena.toml`, `defaults.toml`, anything under `.github/workflows`, `setup.sh`, prompt files, `records/`, or `crates/athena-data/src/records.rs`. The new provenance code reads only existing fields: `Reading.base_commit`, `invocation_seq` and `defaults_sha256`, `Request.received_at`, and the Job dispatch fields. The verifier also runs `cargo test -p athena-data`.
demonstrations.observes: Only the listed files appear, and the athena-data record tests, including the allow-list and round-trip ones, pass unchanged. Grep shows no new record field in `crates/athena-data/src/records.rs`.
demonstrations.fails_without: If a new field had been added to a record without the allow-list and round-trip coverage, `cargo test -p athena-data` would fail on `check_record_file` or the AnyRecord round-trip. If a governance file had been edited, the stat would list it.
demonstrations.seam: The repository diff and the existing athena-data tests (`check_record_file`, AnyRecord round-trip). Existing; nothing is added.

open_questions: User: Do records from jobs written by older Athena builds exist in this repository's history, ones lacking a request record, a reader invocation, or the dispatch fields (`base_commit`, config and defaults hashes, `brief_sha256`, `caps`, `driver`, `athena`)? `records/` is absent from the snapshot, so I could not check, and the new checks refuse such jobs in `athena check --history` (ci.yml:606). If they exist, should the owner list those commits under `[history] exempt` (an athena.toml change this job may not make), or should the producer add an explicit job-id date cutoff? I recommend the exempt list, because a cutoff is bypassed by backdating the id.
